title: Are MCPs Overhyped? A Rant about MCPs — Henry Mao, Smithery
talk_summary: A high-level rant by Smithery's founder about ecosystem problems in MCPs (fragmentation, install friction, security, hosting, observability, monetization) rather than technical techniques. It ends with a demo of an agent chaining a GitHub MCP and a Linear MCP to file a ticket, and a claim that 'agent experience' will matter more than user experience.

takeaways.technique: Tool-discovery layer over many MCP servers
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of hardcoding which MCP servers an agent uses, the agent first calls a 'search servers' function to look up candidate servers in a registry, then connects to the best one plus the task-specific one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It then calls this search servers function which uh looks up for all the servers within SPI3. It connects to the best server.

takeaways.technique: Agent-experience as a design criterion for tool interfaces
takeaways.what_they_do: Frames tool/API design around whether the model will actually call the tool correctly ('how do I know if my tool is going to be called?'), i.e. tool descriptions and schemas are prompt surface, not just API docs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: How do I know if my tool is going to be called? How do I create the best agent experience?

takeaways.technique: Treat third-party MCP/tool installs as an attack surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that installing an MCP from a random GitHub repo with a five-step install can mean installing an insecure server, and that reputation for servers is unsolved.

takeaways.technique: Cross-service task chaining demo (issue tracker + code host)
takeaways.what_they_do: One agent prompt spans two MCPs: search GitHub issues for the most pressing bug, then create a Linear ticket with details and a backlink.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our agent has successfully uh went on GitHub looked for the most pressing issue uh on my GitHub issues and created a linear ticket
